newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga rated AAA by Malaysian agency.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga rated AAA by Malaysian agency.

text.p: National electric utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd has been assigned a top rating of AAA by private bond rating agency Malaysian Rating Corp Bhd (MARC), a statement from MARC said on Tuesday.
MARC said it assigned a short-term rating of MARC-1 to Tenaga, also the highest ranking in that category.
The agency said its ratings apply to Tenaga's long- and short-term senior debt securities and are based on "a very strong implicit sovereign support" for the utility's obligations.
Both the ratings indicate a belief in the company's ability "to repay principal and pay interest on a timely basis is extremely high", MARC said.
MARC noted that the Malaysian government owns about 78 percent of Tenaga's stock and that the electric generator has a "strategic role" in the country's energy policy.
The rating agency also cited Tenaga's strong operating cash flows and growing demand for electricity from a "healthy economy" and expanding customer base.
But MARC also said Tenaga will be tested by huge capital investments to upgrade transmission and distribution facilities as well as "fixed commitments" to independent power producers.
It also said it expects more than 50 percent of Tenaga's capital investments to be funded by internal funds, with the balance to be funded by long-term debt.
"Debt leverage is expected to stabilise at the 40 percent level," MARC said.
Tenaga's cash flow interest coverage ratio is expected to remain strong at 5.5 times "with an improving trend over the medium term", MARC said.
